description: Entering other bodies, knowing others' minds, acting on things at will, divine sight and hearing, memory, radiance and invisibility at will — from concentration of the purified mind.
When the mind is steady in the self, pleasure and pain cease and mastery (vaśitva) arises.
The purified mind shines like a polished mirror, like the sun unclouded, and burns steady like a lamp in a windless place.
In the final renunciation all feelings, perception and knowledge cease; the self become brahman is not perceived and has no mark.
One whose mind in the new birth is joined with the pure (sattva) remembers former births — a 'rememberer of births'.
Dreams of the seen, heard, experienced, longed-for, imagined, portending and doṣa-born.
Uncaused changes in complexion, voice, smell, taste, touch, the senses, mind, conduct and dreams that portend death.
In loss of ojas one is fearful, weak, anxious, with afflicted senses, poor lustre, dejected, dry and emaciated.
Long life, memory, intelligence, health, youth, lustre, complexion and voice, strength of body and senses, success of speech, respect and radiance.

Relief of pain, normal voice and complexion, growth, strength, appetite, good digestion, timely sleep, absence of morbid dreams, easy waking, free passage of wastes and unimpaired mind, intellect and senses.
notes: Ca Vi 8.89 checked in the DCS e-text; no separate teaching entry.

description: Knowledge of the hidden and future, restlessness, intolerance and superhuman action; each class of seizer marked by its own behaviour (the god-seized pure, fragrant, truthful; the ancestor-seized offering rice-balls). Summary only.

Before exogenous insanity: desire to harm gods and brahmins, anger, cruelty, discontent, loss of lustre, being threatened in dreams by gods; in it, strength, valour, memory and knowledge beyond one's own.
The conscious light between the eyebrows, illuminating the world like fire, lightning or sun: supreme bliss, free of conception and affliction, peaceful, self-known.
Those who attained brahmanhood live on, free of passion and hatred, same toward all, their bodies shining, joyful, endowed with the subtle powers (aṇimā and the rest) — the texts' claim.
Swooned mercury (and breath) removes disease, 'dead' revives, bound gives sky-going — the texts' claim; RESTRICTED context.
